items.headline: Lennart Karl out, Ouédraogo called up
items.body: <cite index="1-2">Lennart Karl withdrew injured and was replaced by Assan Ouédraogo on June 5.</cite> <cite index="6-22">Karl suffered a muscle bundle tear in his left thigh</cite> and <cite index="6-26">Nagelsmann described it as a huge shock for Karl and the entire team.</cite>

items.headline: Manuel Neuer fitness status
items.body: <cite index="2-6,2-7">Neuer had a calf injury which kept him out of pre-World Cup friendlies against Finland and the USA, but all indications from Nagelsmann are that the 40-year-old will be fit to face Curaçao on June 14.</cite>

items.headline: Key attacking options available
items.body: <cite index="2-20,2-21">Jamal Musiala has recovered well from the broken leg suffered at the FIFA Club World Cup last summer, with Nagelsmann saying he has been getting better and better.</cite> <cite index="8-1">Kai Havertz has made the squad just in time after an injury-plagued 18 months, and there are genuine gamechangers in the likes of Florian Wirtz and Max Beier.</cite>

items.headline: Strong qualifying campaign
items.body: <cite index="14-1,14-2">Germany finished top of UEFA Group A with 15 points from five wins and one defeat, scoring 16 and conceding three, beating Slovakia, Northern Ireland, and Luxembourg.</cite>

items.headline: Pre-tournament friendlies completed
items.body: <cite index="6-6">Germany defeated the United States 2-1 in Chicago on June 5.</cite> <cite index="22-1">Germany faced Finland in Mainz on May 31 before taking on the USA in Houston.</cite>

items.headline: Morale and coaching stability
items.body: <cite index="25-2">Julian Nagelsmann's side eased through their World Cup qualification group and performed well as the host nation at Euro 2024, perhaps unlucky to fall to Spain in the quarterfinals.</cite> <cite index="25-5">The mood around the camp has shifted considerably under Nagelsmann, and there is genuine optimism heading into North America.</cite>

items.headline: Core formation and style
items.body: <cite index="14-14,14-15">Nagelsmann prefers a flexible 4-2-3-1 formation or variations with high pressing and possession dominance, giving room for central creativity and a flexible attacker (false 9).</cite>

items.headline: Defensive spine
items.body: <cite index="2-9,2-10">Captain Joshua Kimmich plays at right-back under Nagelsmann for Germany, and David Raum has been entrusted to start throughout the World Cup qualification campaign on the left flank.</cite>

items.headline: Central midfield depth
items.body: <cite index="2-16,2-17,2-18">There is uncertainty in central midfield with Leon Goretzka, Aleksandar Pavlović, Felix Nmecha and Angelo Stiller all in the squad, with Nmecha starting both warm-up games alongside Pavlović, though Goretzka's experience may see him line up instead.</cite>

items.headline: Attack: creativity and pace
items.body: <cite index="2-24">Jamal Musiala and Florian Wirtz dovetail well together in the final third, with both exceptional at breaking through deep-lying defences.</cite> <cite index="2-25">Serge Gnabry's injury setback means Leroy Sané could provide width and pace on the right, or Stuttgart's Jamie Leweling could stake his claim for the starting berth.</cite>

items.headline: Favorable group composition
items.body: <cite index="27-5">Germany are in Group E with World Cup first-timers Curaçao, three-time AFCON winners Côte d'Ivoire and South Americans Ecuador, who qualified with the continent's second-best record.</cite>

items.headline: Opener vs Curaçao
items.body: <cite index="24-25">Germany face Curaçao on June 14 in Houston at noon local time (1 p.m. ET).</cite> <cite index="14-11,14-12,14-13">Curaçao are not a consistent team and offer a good start for Germany, having gained their ticket after an impressive display in the CONCACAF qualifiers and making their World Cup debut.</cite>

items.headline: Mid-group test vs Côte d'Ivoire
items.body: <cite index="24-36">Germany face Ivory Coast on June 20 in Toronto at 4 p.m. ET.</cite> <cite index="21-18">Germany has won the teams' two previous meetings: a 3–0 group stage victory at the 2006 FIFA World Cup (which they hosted) and a 4–2 friendly in 2013.</cite>

items.headline: Final group match vs Ecuador
items.body: <cite index="20-4">Ecuador face Germany on June 25 in New York at 22:00 CET.</cite> Ecuador qualified with South America's second-best qualifying record, representing the toughest group opponent.

items.headline: Redemption narrative strong
items.body: <cite index="27-1,27-2">Germany had never failed to advance from consecutive FIFA men's World Cup group stages until four years ago; however, Nagelsmann has instilled a new standard into the squad after their disappointing outings in 2018 and 2022.</cite>

items.headline: Elite squad strength and potential
items.body: <cite index="11-5,11-10,11-11">Germany possess a squad filled with high-quality players, including some of the most exciting young talents in Europe, making them a dangerous opponent despite their recent shortcomings at the big stage.</cite>
